answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a proof-of-quality prism: each identity earns nectar, a decaying reputation score, only when diverse, stake-backed peers independently attest that its work is original and useful. Because attestations are cross-checked and bonded, a farmer cannot just spin up clones that praise each other; every fake identity must produce coherent, distinct, peer-passing work and lock a bond. Like a violet closing at dusk, duplicate or templated answers get rejected and the bond slashed, so the per-identity cost of farming climbs above any payout it could capture.
